top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a mature, independently reproduced achievement (RIKEN, JILA, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) with a clear two-laureate allocation: Katori for the concept and Ye for the many-atom realisation and systematics at the 10^-18 level. It has turned the atom into an almost unperturbed reference and a probe of fundamental physics (redshift over millimetres, constancy of constants), and the citation scope avoids the redefinition of the second. P002 is a genuinely new regime of matter but its interpretation and quantitative theory-experiment agreement are less settled, and the three-name allocation is harder to defend; it still ranks above no award.
recusal_note: Long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-author with Lund and ETH attosecond groups; no apparent direct connection to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, but as an atomic-physics theorist I note a field proximity to precision atomic clocks and would flag it.
